title: Inference Engineer Q&A Pocketbook - draft
content:
TL;DR: One-page, answer-first playbook for sales/SDR/SEs to handle technical discovery, latency/cost objections, and deployment questions during 15–30 minute calls. Keep answers crisp, use scripts, offer follow-ups (benchmarks, runbook links, or a live demo).

Purpose and usage notes:
- Audience: Platform engineers, infra architects, technical buyers, and platform/ML leads.
- When to hand to buyer: after initial architecture fit is confirmed; during technical discovery calls; as a leave-behind after POC kickoff; or attach to RFP responses.
- How to use: memorize the 10 quick-replies, pick 1–2 relevant data points per conversation, and promise a short follow-up measurement (e.g., 3qps latency estimate, cost ballpark).

Quick opening scripts (engineer-facing):
- "We designed Redwood to be predictable across hosted/dedicated/private. For your workload, we’ll pick a model variant and routing policy so you don’t pay for overprovisioning but still hit latency targets."
- "If preservation of PII is required, our Private deployment option keeps inference inside your VPC and integrates with your KMS — we can run a short checklist during POC."

Top 10 engineer FAQs + one-line answers (ready to read aloud):
1) Q: "How do you guarantee latency?"
   A: "We use a GPU-optimized runtime with continuous batching, KV cache, and smart routing; you set a per-route SLO and we route to the best variant or capacity tier to meet it."
2) Q: "What happens during spikes?"
   A: "Autoscaling + burst capacity for Dedicated; Hosted falls back to compatible smaller model variants or cross-region routing per your policy."
3) Q: "Can we run inside our VPC?"
   A: "Yes — Redwood Private runs in your VPC or on-prem with a customer-managed control plane and KMS integration."
4) Q: "How do you limit cost for chat/agent callers?"
   A: "Use prefix/KV caching, request-level caching, token caps, and quantized model variants; our Optimize toolkit recommends the right mix for your throughput profile."
5) Q: "Will outputs regress after a quantized rollout?"
   A: "We recommend canary + targeted evals against a shared prompt set; we surface quality regressions and can auto-rollback to the previous variant."
6) Q: "What telemetry do we get?"
   A: "Token-level cost, per-request latency histograms, per-model quality metrics, and tracing hooks mapped to routes and prompts."
7) Q: "Can I pin a model version?"
   A: "Yes — version pinning and rollout policies are first-class; you control canaries and A/B splits."
8) Q: "How do you handle data retention/compliance?"
   A: "Hosted supports configurable retention windows; Private keeps data inside your environment and integrates with audit logs and HSMs for keys."
9) Q: "Will Redwood work with custom fine-tuned models?"
   A: "We support deploying customer-provided model artifacts and have onboarding guidance for tokenization/kv-cache compatibility."
10) Q: "What SLA do you offer for Dedicated?"
   A: "Dedicated has an SLA tied to reserved capacity with latency targets defined per class; higher tiers include faster autoscaling and regional failover."

Short rebuttals to common pushbacks (one-liners):
- "We can’t open network access": "Private runs entirely on your VPC or air-gapped — we provide an ops package and remote assist for the initial setup."
- "We already self-host": "Great — our unified runtime can replace ad-hoc stacks and reduce token/unit cost while giving you the same control you already have."
- "Latency matters more than cost": "We’ll prioritize low-latency routing, reserve capacity for hot paths, and suggest quantization only for non-critical endpoints."

Measurement snippets to offer as follow-up (pick one):
- "We’ll run a 24-hour micro-benchmark with a 512-token distribution and report p50/p95 latency and per-token cost."
- "We can run a side-by-side: your current endpoint vs Redwood Dedicated with identical sequence-length profiles — expect a 20–60% unit-cost delta depending on batchability."

Checklist for POC kickoff (1–page to drop into calendar invite):
- Identify 2 representative prompts (happy path + worst-case long context).
- Confirm target latency (p50/p95) and QPS for peak and baseline.
- Decide deployment mode (Hosted demo, Dedicated trial, or Private POC).
- Confirm data security constraints (PII, retention, KMS).
- Identify rollout success metrics (latency, token cost, quality eval thresholds).

Live demo recipe (10–12 minutes):
1) 90s: Quick product intro + one-sentence differentiation (unified runtime + cost controls).
2) 3m: Show Console route dashboard (latency by model, token cost).
3) 3m: Run a short live generation vs current endpoint (same prompt) and show p50/p95 changes live.
4) 2m: Show an Optimize suggestion (quantization or batching) and expected cost delta.
5) 1m: Agree on next steps: POC measurement, timeline, and required access.

Objection escalation map (who to pull in):
- Security/compliance: Nate Flores (security) or Lena Moretti (private deploy PM).
- Deep inference perf tuning: Ravi Patel (serving-runtime lead).
- Enterprise contracts/reserved capacity: Priya Singh (sales ops).

Props & quick references (links to send after call):
- Short bench: 512-token micro-bench (p50/p95 + cost per 1k tokens).
- Private deployment checklist (network/KMS checklist).
- Quality regression playbook (canary + rollback steps).

Unresolved scribbles (notes to product/eng):
- Add a "fast-fallback" flag for route-level canaries (requested by FinServ pilot).
- Make an SDK snippet that auto-generates kv-cache warmers for chat sessions.
- Dashboard: expose top-10 prompt clusters causing highest per-token cost in last 24h.

Short session prep for SEs (bullet list):
- Read the one-pager before calls.
- Bring the POC checklist to the discovery call and walk through it.
- Use the demo recipe as a script; time-box each section.

Appendix: Suggested courtroom-ready metrics to quote (numbers are ballpark — run follow-up bench for client-specific estimates):
- Typical p50 latency, 512 tokens, dedicated GPU pool: 35–120 ms (model-dependent).
- Typical p95 latency, 512 tokens, dedicated GPU pool: 90–350 ms.
- Unit cost delta: hosting vs naive self-hosting: -20% to -60% depending on batching and cache hit rate.

Footer: quick contacts and Slack handles: @ava.chen (go-to-market), @ravi.patel (serving-runtime), @lena.moretti (private deployments).

(End of pocketbook)
